newsitem.title: CHINA: China says nationalism sharpens military.
newsitem.headline: China says nationalism sharpens military.

text.p: China, awash in a tide of fervent nationalism, said on Tuesday its recent patriotism drive had sharpened the combat skills of its armed forces.

Patriotic education campaigns in the military had "effectively strengthened the cohesiveness of troops and raised their combat strength", said the People's Daily, mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party.
Beijing has seen its traditional Marxist ideology dissolve under rapid economic reforms and has sought to fill the gap with nationalism.
Military exercises off Taiwan in March greatly boosted patriotic fervour amongst troops and spurred their fighting will, the newspaper said.
Beijing has regarded Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a rebel province since the end of the civil war in 1949 and vows to take the island by force if Taipei declares independence.
Soldiers had taken part in competitions to show their love of the motherland and display their selfless spirit, the newspaper said.
Troops and officers would be taught to subordinate personal ambition to the socialist cause, it said.

The newspaper urged the navy to foster a spirit of "love the islands, love the ships and love the ocean", while the air force should embrace the mottoes "love the motherland" and "love the blue sky", it said.
